summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of TIPS placement, was admitted due to coffee ground emesis and melena concerning for an upper gastrointestinal bleed. His hemoglobin was 6.2 g/dL on presentation, and he received three units of packed red blood cells. An EGD revealed an esophageal ulcer and portal hypertensive gastropathy without active bleeding. He underwent a large volume paracentesis with removal of 6 liters of fluid; microbiology showed no infection. His hyponatremia fluctuated but remained asymptomatic. He was managed with pantoprazole, octreotide, and continued home medications including lactulose and rifaximin. He remained stable, with no rebleeding, and was discharged home with plans for follow-up EGD in three months, hepatology follow-up, and monitoring for signs of recurrence.
